title.value: Re-Weighted Softmax Cross-Entropy to Control Forgetting in Federated Learning
title.justification: The title reflects the main focus of the paper, which is the modification of the softmax cross-entropy to tackle the problem of forgetting in federated learning.
title.quote: Re-Weighted Softmax Cross-Entropy to Control Forgetting in Federated Learning

extractions.description: The paper presents a method for improving federated learning by addressing client forgetting through a re-weighted softmax cross-entropy approach. This method aims to handle the data heterogeneity problem across clients by maintaining model accuracy on different client's data and reducing local client drift during training. The method was evaluated on various datasets demonstrating improved performance over standard federated algorithms.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central theme of the paper is improving federated learning processes, which is related to machine learning optimization rather than a direct focus on Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Federated Learning (FL) is a distributed machine learning paradigm in which a shared global model is learned from a decentralized set of data located at a number of independent client nodes.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not directly address any specific topics within Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development, focusing instead on a machine learning optimization problem.
primary_category.quote: We show that individual client models experience a catastrophic forgetting with respect to data from other clients and propose an efficient approach that modifies the cross-entropy objective on a perclient basis by re-weighting the softmax logits prior to computing the loss.

primary_sub_category.justification: As there are no clear applications or connections to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development, no specific sub-category applies.
primary_sub_category.quote: Our method is particularly beneficial under the most challenging federated learning settings where data heterogeneity is high and client participation in each round is low.

new_primary_category.justification: There is no need for a new primary category as the content strictly deals with federated learning insights unrelated to sustainable development.
new_primary_category.quote: This approach shields classes outside a client’s label set from abrupt representation change and we empirically demonstrate it can alleviate client forgetting and provide consistent improvements to standard federated learning algorithms.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The existing taxonomy of sub-categories does not need expansion or alteration since the paper's primary contributions are within machine learning optimization, unrelated to climate or ecological concerns.
